title: SII Vol. 14 No. 251 — Tenkarai
location_detail: On a stone set up in the courtyard of the Mulasthanesvara temple
date_text: This record of Jatavarman Srivallabha is dated in the 20 + 1st year of his reign
summary: It mentions the merchant-guild of Ayyapolil and appears to record certain rules framed by them in regard to the social classes Valangai and Idangai

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 252 — Tiruppattur
location_detail: On the east wall of the mandapa in the Tiruttalisvara temple
summary: This inscription belongs to the 21st year of Tribhuvanachakravartin Srivallabhadeva, and registers a gift of 50 sheep by Rajendrasolan Keralan alias [Nishadarajan for burning a lamp in the temple of Sritali-Paramesvara at Tirupputtur

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 253 — Sivapuri
location_detail: On the south wall of the second prakara of the Svayamprakasa temple
summary: This record of the 21st year of Tribhuvanachakravartin Srivallabha registers a gift of land by Tiruchchirramablam-udiayan Tiruvenkadattalvan of Marudur, a merchant of Aruviyur alias Desi-uyyavanda-pattanam for the kitchen expenses of the temple of Tiruttandonri-udaiyar at Nripasekhara-chaturvedimang

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 254 — Kuruvitturai
location_detail: On the north wall of the Chitraratha-vallabha-Perumal temple
summary: This record of Jatavarman Srivallabha dated on the 200th day of the 22nd year of his reign purports to have been issued while the king was seated on the pallikkattil called Pandiyerayan in the theatre (natakasalai) with the palace at Madurai

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 255 — Kuruvitturai
location_detail: On the north wall of the Chitrarathavallabha-Perumal temple
date_text: These two complementary inscriptions are dated in the 22nd year of an unspecified king who laws evidently Jatavarman Srivallabha
summary: One of them is an order (olai) issued by Kalingarajan to the Srivaishnavas of the temple intimating the fact that the lands mentioned in

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 254
location_detail: above belonging to the Chakrattalvar temple were made tax-free, and the second gives publicity to this exemption granted on these lands

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 256 — Sermadevi
location_detail: On the south wall of the Ramasvamin temple
date_text: This is an incomplete inscription of the 22 + 1st year of the king and it stops after the mentioning the name of the village

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 257 — Tiruttangal
location_detail: On the east wall of the mandapa in the Ninranarayana-Perumal temple
date_text: This record of Srivallabha dated in the year opposite to the 22nd year of his reign contains the date 22nd year and  40th day at the end
summary: The king while seated on the throne named Kalingattaraiyan in his palace at Madurai issued this order to the mulaparishad of Tiruttangal to the effect that this village which had originally been a devadna-brahmadeya of Karunilakkudi-nadu and had subsequently been made tax-paying was to be restored t

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 258 — Tiruttangal
location_detail: On left side of the entrance into the Sengamala
date_text: This is an incomplete inscription dated in the 23rd year of the king
summary: Nachchiyar shrine in the Ninranarayana-Perumal temple

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 259 — Sivapuri
location_detail: On the east wall of the second prakara of the Svayamprakasa temple
summary: This record dated in the 24th year of Tribhuvanachakravartin Srivallabha registers a gift of land and a house-site for the maintenance of a matha at Sivapuri called the Alagiya-manavalan by Alagiya-manavalan Udiyanambi alias A agaiman of Tirunallur, a merchant of Aruviyur alias Desi-uyyavanda-pattan

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 260 — Sivapuri
location_detail: On the south wall of the second prakara in the Svayamprakasa temple
summary: Dated in the 25th year of the king, this inscription registers a gift of land by the chieftain Rajendrasolan Keralan alias Devar Nishadarajan alias Alalasundarapperumal for the expenses of the temple of Tiruttandonrisvaram-Udaiyar

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 261 — Sivapuri
location_detail: On the south wall of the Svayamprakasa temple
date_text: This inscription is dated in the year opposite to the 26th year of the reign of Srivallabha
summary: It is incomplete and appears to register gift of money by a brahmana lady of Sivapuri which was invested on the purchase of some land named Sikhandivasakkal, for providing worship to god Tiruttandorisvaram-Udaiyar at Nripasekhara-chaturvedimangalam

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 262 — Vikkiramangalam
location_detail: On the two doorjambs of a ruined shrine near the Marudappar temple
summary: At the request of Kallingarajna, the lands in Sekkali were reconstituted into a new village called Srivallavanallur and given as tax-free devadana to the temple of Madurodaya-Isvaram-Udaiyar at Vikkiramasolapuram

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 263 — Tirumalaipuram
location_detail: On a pillar in the rock-cut cave
summary: This damaged inscription of Tirbhuvanachakravartin Srivallabha states that the king was seated on the Pandiyarajan in the Alagiyapandiyan hall in the palace to the north of Solantaka-chaturvedimangalam in Paganur-kuram and issued the order to the sabhaiyar of Viranarayanamangalam in Tugavur-kurram a

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 264 — Dalapatisamudram
location_detail: On the base of the verandah in the Tirunagesvara temple
date_text: This record belongs to the reign of Jatavarman Srivallabha though it is not specifically dated in any regnal year
summary: The king is stated to have been seated on the bed-stead (pallikkattil) called Kalingattaraiyan in the bed-chamber (palliyaraikkudam) in the northern wing of the palace at Rajendrasolapuram in the subdivision Rajasingan-kulakkil, in Madurodaya-valanadu while issuing this record

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 265 — Sendamangalam
location_detail: On the south wall of the central shrine in the Kailasanatha temple
summary: This record of Jatavarman Srivallabha is damaged and so its date is lost

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 266 — Kunnakkudi
location_detail: On the north wall of the first cave
summary: This inscription of Srivallabha dated in the 4th year records the gift of land for a lamp by Adavi of Tirukkunrakkudi to god Tirumalaiyudaiya-nayanar

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 267 — Kilappavur
location_detail: On the west and south walls of the central shrine in the Tiruvalisvara Temple
summary: This inscription commences with the prasasti of Tirumadandaiyum Jayamadandaiyum, etc., of Jatavarman Srivallabha and records the gift of land made tax free in Pattamangalam separated from Kurunganam alias Telingakulakala-chaturvedimangalam to the god of the temple of Tirukkapalisvaram in Pagur alias
